concepts.label: backhaul-link
concepts.gloss: A transport link that terminates at a site gateway and carries aggregated RAN traffic from one or more radio cells toward the core or transport network (the site-level uplink between the cell site and the network).
concepts.example: bh-441 (site-to-core): the site-to-core transport link that presents at csg-441 and serves radio cells 441-A and 441-B, carrying their user and control traffic to the core.

concepts.label: site-gateway
concepts.gloss: The site gateway or demarcation device at a cell site that terminates a backhaul link and provides the boundary/interface between the RAN site and the wider transport/network cloud.
concepts.example: csg-441: the cell-site gateway at site 441 which the link bh-441 terminates on, exposing the site's RAN-facing interfaces to the transport domain.

concepts.label: backhaul-marking
concepts.gloss: The DiffServ-based QoS marking profile applied on a backhaul link that classifies packets into transport treatment classes (e.g., EF, AF41, default) for queuing and forwarding across the transport.
concepts.example: On bh-441 the backhaul-marking 'EF / AF41 / default' maps real-time voice to EF, priority data to AF41 and everything else to the default PHB for that link.

concepts.label: backhaul-capacity
concepts.gloss: The provisioned or committed throughput (rate) allocated to a backhaul link, expressing the link's capacity or committed information rate for carrying RAN traffic.
concepts.example: bh-441 has backhaul-capacity '8 Gbit/s committed', meaning the transport is provisioned to carry up to 8 Gbit/s of committed traffic for the site.

concepts.label: backhaul-mtu
concepts.gloss: The maximum transmission unit configured on a backhaul transport link that determines the largest frame/payload size allowed on that link and thus affects framing and fragmentation between site and core.
concepts.example: bh-441 configured with 'MTU 1600' allows jumbo frames up to 1600 bytes across the site-to-core link terminating at csg-441.

concepts.label: radio-cell
concepts.gloss: A radio coverage sector or logical cell at a site which is served by a backhaul link and within which radio sessions and UE attachments are established.
concepts.example: cell 441-A: a radio sector at site 441 served by bh-441 that can host RRC sessions (for example rrc-session #55) and carry subscriber traffic over the backhaul.

concepts.label: rrc-session
concepts.gloss: An individual RRC (radio resource control) session representing a UE's connected radio-layer state and control context within a particular cell.
concepts.example: rrc-session #55 (cell 441-A): an active RRC connection for a subscriber attached to cell 441-A, mapped to that cell and using the site's backhaul for user-plane traffic.

concepts.label: beacon-tag-7
concepts.gloss: A vendor‑specific opaque attribute (Beacon proprietary tag 7) attached to a backhaul link used to carry implementation-specific metadata or flags that the general model does not interpret.
concepts.example: beacon-tag-7=0x2 on bh-441: the site gateway csg-441 reports proprietary attribute 7 with value 0x2 for link bh-441, indicating a vendor-defined per-link flag or configuration state.
